newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Zaire rebel says Mobutu must go by Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel says Mobutu must go by Saturday.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko must abandon Zaire by Saturday or rebel forces will enter Kinshasa and capture him, a senior rebel official was quoted as saying on Thursday.

Rebel Justice "Commissioner-General" Mwenze Kongolo issued the warning in remarks to Portuguese news agency Lusa in Cabinda as rebel leader Laurent Kabila left the Angolan enclave for South Africa where he is due to meet President Nelson Mandela who has been seeking to negotiate a peace deal.
Kongolo said that only Mobutu's surrender would ensure a peaceful end to the seven-month conflict which has carried rebel forces to within striking distance of Kinshasa.
If no deal were done, rebel forces would enter Kinshasa and Mobutu would run "the risk of being captured ... if he insists on remaining in power until Saturday," the agency quoted Kongolo as saying.
Mandela invited Kabila for more talks after the rebel leader failed to show up for a South African-brokered meeting with Mobutu in Congo on Thursday, alleging lack of security.

South Africa was reportedly proposing an all-party transitional authority to run Zaire until elections could be held. Mobutu should resign within 24 hours of the accord being signed, a report on South African state radio said.
But Kongolo appeared to dismiss any chance of groups' loyal to Mobutu taking part in the transition.

"The only way out of the crisis is for Mobutu to hand over power to the armed rebellion which will form a transitional government together with other forces fighting for the same cause," Kongolo told Lusa.
This period of transition should last at least two years, he added.
